title: Problem 1
statement_text: Which graph classes have bounded domination-to-2-independence ratio?
context_text: The domination number $\gamma(G)$ is the minimum size of a set $D\subseteq V(G)$ such that every vertex is in $D$ or has a neighbor in $D$; the $2$-independence number $\alpha_2(G)$ is the maximum size of a set of vertices pairwise at distance greater than two (equivalently, of a packing of pairwise disjoint closed neighborhoods). Clearly $\alpha_2(G)\le\gamma(G)$, and the fractional relaxations of the two parameters are dual linear programs with equal value, computable in polynomial time; so when $\gamma/\alpha_2$ is bounded both parameters are approximated by their common fractional relaxation, whereas both are hard to approximate in general. The domination-to-2-independence ratio of a class $\mathcal{G}$ is $\sup_{G\in\mathcal{G}}\gamma(G)/\alpha_2(G)$, and $\mathcal{G}$ has domination tied to 2-independence if $\gamma(G)\le h(\alpha_2(G))$ for all $G\in\mathcal{G}$ and some function $h$. The ratio is known to be bounded for trees, strongly chordal and dually chordal graphs (ratio 1), outerplanar graphs, 2-degenerate graphs, unit disk graphs, graphs of maximum degree $\Delta$, all proper minor-closed classes, graphs of bounded twin-width and graphs of bounded weak 2-coloring number (hence all classes of bounded expansion); on the other hand, Cartesian products of cliques, bipartite 3-degenerate graphs and split graphs are not even tied. The paper answers the question for monotone classes (closed under subgraphs) of bounded average degree: such a class has bounded ratio if and only if the slopes of the cascades it contains are bounded, where a cascade is a graph $H$ properly colored with colors v, e, d such that every e-vertex has exactly two v-neighbors and one d-neighbor and there are no other edges, its foundation $F$ is the graph on the v-vertices in which two are adjacent when they have a common e-neighbor, and its slope is $|\mathrm{v}|/\max(\alpha(F),|\mathrm{d}|)$. The question remains open for hereditary (not monotone) classes and for dense classes.
paper_title: Characterization of sparse monotone graph classes with bounded domination-to-2-independence ratio

title: Problem 2
statement_text: Which graph classes have domination tied to 2-independence?
context_text: The domination number $\gamma(G)$ is the minimum size of a set $D\subseteq V(G)$ such that every vertex is in $D$ or has a neighbor in $D$; the $2$-independence number $\alpha_2(G)$ is the maximum size of a set of vertices pairwise at distance greater than two (equivalently, of a packing of pairwise disjoint closed neighborhoods). Clearly $\alpha_2(G)\le\gamma(G)$, and the fractional relaxations of the two parameters are dual linear programs with equal value, computable in polynomial time; so when $\gamma/\alpha_2$ is bounded both parameters are approximated by their common fractional relaxation, whereas both are hard to approximate in general. The domination-to-2-independence ratio of a class $\mathcal{G}$ is $\sup_{G\in\mathcal{G}}\gamma(G)/\alpha_2(G)$, and $\mathcal{G}$ has domination tied to 2-independence if $\gamma(G)\le h(\alpha_2(G))$ for all $G\in\mathcal{G}$ and some function $h$. Bounded ratio is exactly the case where $h$ can be taken linear, so this is a relaxation of the question which classes have bounded domination-to-2-independence ratio; the authors remark that it seems non-trivial even for sparse monotone classes. Cartesian products of cliques, bipartite 3-degenerate graphs and split graphs do not have domination tied to 2-independence, nor does the class of graphs of maximum average degree at most $d$ for any $d\ge 6$ (for $d<6$ this class has bounded ratio, as the authors show). The paper characterizes bounded ratio for monotone classes of bounded average degree, but this does not settle the tied version: for $k\ge 3$ and $d>0$, the class of graphs of maximum average degree at most $d$ containing no $1$-subdivision of $K_k$ as a subgraph has domination tied to 2-independence, yet for $k\ge5$, $d\ge6$ it has unbounded ratio.
paper_title: Characterization of sparse monotone graph classes with bounded domination-to-2-independence ratio
